ESV.2: “Today also my complaint is bitter;  my hand is heavy on account of my groaning.
ESV.3: Oh, that I knew where I might find him, that I might come even to his seat!
ESV.4: I would lay my case before him and fill my mouth with arguments.
ESV.5: I would know what he would answer me and understand what he would say to me.
ESV.6: Would he contend with me in the greatness of his power? No; he would pay attention to me.
ESV.7: There an upright man could argue with him, and I would be acquitted forever by my judge.
ESV.8: “Behold, I go forward, but he is not there, and backward, but I do not perceive him;
ESV.9: on the left hand when he is working, I do not behold him; he turns to the right hand, but I do not see him.
ESV.10: But he knows the way that I take; when he has tried me, I shall come out as gold.
ESV.11: My foot has held fast to his steps; I have kept his way and have not turned aside.
ESV.12: I have not departed from the commandment of his lips; I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my portion of food.
ESV.13: But he is unchangeable,  and who can turn him back? What he desires, that he does.
ESV.14: For he will complete what he appoints for me, and many such things are in his mind.
ESV.15: Therefore I am terrified at his presence; when I consider, I am in dread of him.
ESV.16: God has made my heart faint; the Almighty has terrified me;
ESV.17: yet I am not silenced because of the darkness, nor because thick darkness covers my face.

NLT.2:
“My complaint today is still a bitter one,
and I try hard not to groan aloud.
NLT.3:
If only I knew where to find God,
I would go to his court.
NLT.4:
I would lay out my case
and present my arguments.
NLT.5:
Then I would listen to his reply
and understand what he says to me.
NLT.6:
Would he use his great power to argue with me?
No, he would give me a fair hearing.
NLT.7:
Honest people can reason with him,
so I would be forever acquitted by my judge.
NLT.8:
I go east, but he is not there.
I go west, but I cannot find him.
NLT.9:
I do not see him in the north, for he is hidden.
I look to the south, but he is concealed.
NLT.10:
“But he knows where I am going.
And when he tests me, I will come out as pure as gold.
NLT.11:
For I have stayed on God’s paths;
I have followed his ways and not turned aside.
NLT.12:
I have not departed from his commands,
but have treasured his words more than daily food.
NLT.13:
But once he has made his decision, who can change his mind?
Whatever he wants to do, he does.
NLT.14:
So he will do to me whatever he has planned.
He controls my destiny.
NLT.15:
No wonder I am so terrified in his presence.
When I think of it, terror grips me.
NLT.16:
God has made me sick at heart;
the Almighty has terrified me.
NLT.17:
Darkness is all around me;
thick, impenetrable darkness is everywhere.

NIV.2:
“Even today my complaint is bitter;
his hand is heavy in spite of my groaning.
NIV.3:
If only I knew where to find him;
if only I could go to his dwelling!
NIV.4:
I would state my case before him
and fill my mouth with arguments.
NIV.5:
I would find out what he would answer me,
and consider what he would say.
NIV.6:
Would he oppose me with great power?
No, he would not press charges against me.
NIV.7:
There an upright man could present his case before him,
and I would be delivered forever from my judge.
NIV.8:
“But if I go to the east, he is not there;
if I go to the west, I do not find him.
NIV.9:
When he is at work in the north, I do not see him;
when he turns to the south, I catch no glimpse of him.
NIV.10:
But he knows the way that I take;
when he has tested me, I will come forth as gold.
NIV.11:
My feet have closely followed his steps;
I have kept to his way without turning aside.
NIV.12:
I have not departed from the commands of his lips;
I have treasured the words of his mouth more than my daily bread.
NIV.13:
“But he stands alone, and who can oppose him?
He does whatever he pleases.
NIV.14:
He carries out his decree against me,
and many such plans he still has in store.
NIV.15:
That is why I am terrified before him;
when I think of all this, I fear him.
NIV.16:
God has made my heart faint;
the Almighty has terrified me.
NIV.17:
Yet I am not silenced by the darkness,
by the thick darkness that covers my face.

MSG.2:
"I'm not letting up—I'm standing my ground.
My complaint is legitimate.
God has no right to treat me like this—
it isn't fair!
MSG.3:
If I knew where on earth to find him,
I'd go straight to him.
MSG.4:
I'd lay my case before him face-to-face,
give him all my arguments firsthand.
MSG.5:
I'd find out exactly what he's thinking,
discover what's going on in his head.
MSG.6:
Do you think he'd dismiss me or bully me?
No, he'd take me seriously.
MSG.7:
He'd see a straight-living man standing before him;
my Judge would acquit me for good of all charges.
MSG.8:
"I travel East looking for him—I find no one;
then West, but not a trace;
MSG.9:
I go North, but he's hidden his tracks;
then South, but not even a glimpse.
MSG.10:
"But he knows where I am and what I've done.
He can cross-examine me all he wants, and I'll pass the test
with honors.
MSG.11:
I've followed him closely, my feet in his footprints,
not once swerving from his way.
MSG.12:
I've obeyed every word he's spoken,
and not just obeyed his advice—I've treasured it.
MSG.13:
"But he is singular and sovereign. Who can argue with him?
He does what he wants, when he wants to.
MSG.14:
He'll complete in detail what he's decided about me,
and whatever else he determines to do.
MSG.15:
Is it any wonder that I dread meeting him?
Whenever I think about it, I get scared all over again.
MSG.16:
God makes my heart sink!
God Almighty gives me the shudders!
MSG.17:
I'm completely in the dark,
I can't see my hand in front of my face.
